NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS’ MINUTES 
TUESDAY, November 12, 2013 
 
Present: Sylvia Allen, Supervisor; Dawnafe Whitesinger, Supervisor; David Tenney, Supervisor; Jesse 
Thompson, Supervisor; and Jonathan M. Nez, Chairman were present in person.  
9:02 a.m.  Call To Order: Pledge of Allegiance and Invocation led by Supervisor Thompson.  
Chairman Nez welcomed all to the Board meeting and thanked all of the veterans for their service to this 
Country.  
 
CALL TO THE PUBLIC: There were no public comments. 
 
CONSENT AGENDA:  a) Juvenile Probation Report October 2013 b) Clerk of Superior Court Report October 
2013 c) Justice Court Reports: Holbrook Precinct #1, October; Winslow Precinct #2, October; Snowflake Precinct 
#3, October; Kayenta Precinct #4, October; Show Low Precinct #5, October; and Pinetop -Lakeside Precinct #6, 
October 2013 d) Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000 for September and October 2013 e) Contract addendum 
with Levi, Ray Shoup for consultant services for implementation of content management system in the additional 
amount of $11,950 f) Agreement signed by County Manager per Board of Supervisors Resolution : Work order 
quote from CCI for Onsite Deskside RealWare Version 5 training g) Resolution Number 32 -13, urging the 
Arizona Legislature to discontinue sweeps of Highway User Revenue Funds (HURF) and to restore funding to 
pre-sweep levels h) Letter to Governor Janice K. Brewer regarding Navajo County Statewide Legislative Priories 
for 2014 i) Resolution Number 33-13, extending the agreement between the Town of Pinetop Lakeside and the 
Navajo County Government for the Lease of Justice Court Facilities j) Letter to Patrick A. Bray, Executive Vice 
President of the Arizona Cattle Growers’ Association, regarding adding Navajo County as signator to the 
Stakeholder Letter to U.S. Fish and Wildlife k) Appreciation letter to the Honorable Gregory Mendoza and the 
Gila River Indian Community l) Letter to U.S. Forest Supervisor Earl Stewart in regard to new prohibitions on 
parking trailers: Supervisor Thompson made a motion to authorize the Chairman to sign the items in the consent 
agenda as presented; motion seconded by Supervisor Tenney. Vote unanimous approving the motion.  
BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
a. Crowning of 2013-14 Navajo County Rodeo Queen: Chairman Nez and Supervisor Allen crowned the 
2013-2014 Navajo County Rodeo Queen Ms. Randi Ann Rima. 
b. Consideration and possible approval of a Statement of Support by Navajo County for the Employer 
Support of the Guard and Reserve : Jack Latham addressed the Board of Supervisors requesting Navajo 
County’s support of the Guard and Reserve and to recognize, honor and enforce the Uniformed Services 
Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA). Mr. Latham reported  the Arizona Supreme 
Court just issued a website for veterans to help answer legal questions and to use as a veteran’s guide to 
find the resources they need.   Supervisor Tenney made a motion to issue a Statement of Support by 
Navajo County for the  Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve ; motion seconded by Supervisor 
Thompson. Vote unanimous approving the motion.  
HUMAN RESOURCES : Consideration and possible approval of Personnel Actions: Kimberly Eavenson  
presented the 27 item personnel action report. Supervisor Tenney made a motion  to approve the personnel 
action report as presented; motion seconded by Supervisor Thompson. Vote unanimous approving the motion.

<!-- page 2 -->
Board of Supervisor Minutes 11-12-2013 
    Page 2 of 4 
 
      COUNTY ATTORNEY: Consideration and possible approval of FY14 Victims’ Rights Program Award 
Agreement: Lynda Young reviewed the FY14 Victims’ Rights Program Award Agreement. Ms. Young indicated 
this grant pays for a notificatio n clerk, as well as legal staff and  to notify victims of their rights during criminal 
proceedings. Supervisor Whitesinger made a motion  to approve the FY14 Victims’ Rights Program Award 
Agreement; motion seconded by Supervisor Allen. Vote unanimous approving the motion.  
      JUVENILE PROBATION: Consideration and possible acceptance of the award for the Drug Free Communities 
Grant Proposal submitted by the Navajo County Drug Project: Item pulled.  
PUBLIC WORKS:  
a. Consideration and possible approval of Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment to #B13 -06-021 
Construction Manager -at-Risk contract for the New Public Works Complex with Haydon Building 
Corporation: Homero Vela discussed the Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment to #B13 -06-021 
Construction Manager-at-Risk contract for the New Public Works Comp lex with Haydon Building 
Corporation. Mr. Vela stated this agreement establishes the GMP in the amount of $4,999,046. Fritz 
Behrhorst, Vice President with Haydon Building Corporation addressed the Board and indicated his 
company is try ing to keep the work local. Tom Wells, Project Manager  for the Haydon Building 
Corporation, then introduced himself and extended his appreciation to the Board. Supervisor Allen  
inquired about the deadline and penalties if the project is not finished on time. Mr. Vela indicated that 
construction will begin mid -December 2013 and completed in October of 2014. He stated  there are no 
penalties for late construction, however they are committed to the timeframe. Supervisor Tenney made 
a motion to approve the Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment to #B13-06-021 Construction Manager-
at-Risk contract for the New Public Works Complex with Haydon Building Corporation; motion seconded 
by Supervisor Allen. Vote unanimous approving the motion.  
b. Consideration and possible approval of the use of ice melt on an experimental basis on roads and an anti-
ice product on parking lots for the 2013/2014 winter season: Russ McCray and Bret Starns addressed the 
Board regarding a trial run of the use of granular ice melt mixed with cinders on select roads to evaluate 
blended ice melt/cinders in terms of cost and effectiveness. The cost for using the blended material on 
these roads for an entire snow season is determined to be $9,000.00 . Also the Public Works Staff would 
like to use anti -icing products in parking lots to minimize the potential for slips and falls.  The cost for 
using anti-icing is approximately $10,000 .00 per season. Public Works Director Homer Vela  indicated 
that the Rock Salt which will be used is already used by most states and told the Board the product would 
have a low impact on the environment. Mr. Vela  stated they are looking to reduce accidents across the 
county. Mr. McCray indicated that each road will be assessed at the end of the snow season. Supervisor 
Whitesinger made a motion to approve the use of ice melt on an experimental basis on roads and an anti-
ice product on parking lots for the 2013/2014 winter season ; motion seconded by Supervisor Tenney. 
Vote unanimous approving the motion.  
c. NAVAJO COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT Board of Directors Session: Consent Agenda: 
Consideration and possible approval of the Community Rating System Recertification Letter: Supervisor 
Tenney made a motion  to enter into the  Navajo County  Flood Control District Board of Directors 
Session; motion seconded by Supervisor Thompson. Vote unanimous approving the motion. Supervisor 
Tenney made a motion to approve the Consent Agenda as presented ; motion seconded by Supervisor 
Whitesinger. Vote unanimous approving the motion . Supervisor Tenney made a motion to return to 
regular session; motion seconded by Supervisor Thompson. Vote unanimous approving the motion.

<!-- page 3 -->
Board of Supervisor Minutes 11-12-2013 
    Page 3 of 4 
 
      COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE : Report from Board members, County Attorney and County Manager : 
Chairman Nez reported he will attend the NPC flag raising ceremony today.  Chairman Nez spoke about the 
partnerships with the graveling projects. He reported on the Veterans D ay event at Oljato  which he attended . 
Chairman Nez thanked Sheriff Clark and Judge Hatch for attending the Domestic Violence meeting.  He stated 
the Navajo Nation Council just went through their fall session which  concluded in three days. Chairman Nez 
stated he had four legislative bills on the council session agenda. He reported the Council is considering putting 
a 2% tax on junk food because they acknowledge that there is a need for healthy living and making better choices 
for food on the Navajo Nation especially because of the high rates of obesity and diabetes. Chairman Nez shared 
his personal time for the 50 kilometers race in Boulder City. He indicated the Brooklyn Marathon is going to be 
this Saturday. Chairman Nez stated it is his goal to  run all 50 States. Vice Chairman Thompson reported on 
the Economic Community Development Summit which was put on by Senator Carlyle W. Begay; he also attended 
the Hopi Veterans event parade and spoke at the Leupp’s Veterans Day program. He reported he and the Winslow 
Dine Residents met with the Winslow Mayor and the Navajo Nation regarding the ownership of lands. At 9:53 
a.m. Chairman Nez left the meeting. Supervisor Tenney reported on the Show Low VFW Veteran’s Dinner 
where he participated. He reported he spent time with Andy Tobin , Speaker of the House regarding his support 
and firm commitment for the full restoration of HURF. He indicated he will be meeting with President Biggs of 
the Senate next week in regards to the same commitment.  Supervisor Whitesinger reported she spoke at a Child 
Find Conference. She also spoke at the White Mountain Apache Women’s Conference and stated she continues 
to work with the Sunrise Board which now has a new general manager . She indicated  she participated at the 
Domestic V iolence Fatality Review Board with County Attorney Brad Carlyon. Supervisor Whitesinger  
indicated she went to  the Show Low , Pinetop joint C ouncil meeting and also attended along with Supervisor 
Thompson, the Economic Development Summit  which covered building new Tribal  enterprises. She reported 
she had the opportunity to speak with many children who are facing difficult circumstances within their families. 
Supervisor Allen spoke of the meeting she had with President Biggs. She reported she spoke at the White 
Mountain Lakes Community Center meeting. Supervisor Allen expressed appreciation to Mr. Homero Vela and 
the Public Works staff for their efforts to get a permit for  the installation of a street light in the White Mountain 
Lakes community. She reported she attended the 100 year dedication of the Snowflake Academy and she reported 
on another clean up in Woodruff. Supervisor Allen stated she will attend the Twin Knolls Transportation Meeting 
open house at the Snowflake City Council and she will be speaking at Taylor City Council meeting. Supervisor 
Tenney and the Board sang Happy Birthday to Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board. Vice-Chairman Thompson 
thanked Mrs. Buckley for the outstanding work she does for the Board. Mr. Vela, Assistant County Manager and 
Public Works Director welcomed everyone to attend the Thanksgiving Progressive Dinner starting at 11:30 a.m. 
in the Code Talkers Conference room and the cafeteria. Mr. Vela also reported Holbrook will be hosting the Red 
Dog meeting at the Public Works Department and that the Emergency Management meeting in Flagstaff at Twin 
Arrows Casino, are both on Friday. He then invited all to attend the Groundbreaking Ceremony for the new Public 
Works Complex at 10:30 a.m. at SR 77 & SR 377. 
 
      ADJOURN: At 10:08 a.m. Supervisor Tenney made a motion to adjourn; motion seconded by Supervisor 
Whitesinger. Vote unanimous approving the motion.
